message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and my only trade today, leaving the $50,000 cash balance and existing 100 MSFT shares untouched). The quote at the time was $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so my limit was essentially at market. Fundamentally, Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year FY2024 net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge) — all confirmed against the 10-K filed 2024-11-01. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, with services growing double digits. Given solid growth, a strong services mix, and a valuation near $222 (~36x FY24 EPS), I sized a modest starter position rather than a full allocation, keeping room to add on weakness within the mandate.
